entities.summary:
Chares of Mytilene (b. 350 BCE, Mytilene) was a political leader or statesperson of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Mytilene. Known in the fields of journalists & chroniclers.

As a member of the aristocracy, Chares of Mytilene played a pivotal role in shaping Mytilene's governance, collaborating with other influential figures to establish a democratic system.

His leadership was marked by several key achievements, including the establishment of a robust system of governance, the promotion of the arts, and the development of infrastructure projects such as the construction of a new harbor.

Despite his contributions, Chares of Mytilene's legacy is somewhat ambiguous, with some historians viewing him as a key figure in the rise of democracy, while others see him as a product of his time, reflecting the complexities and contradictions of the Classical era.

One striking statistic that highlights the significance of Chares of Mytilene's leadership is the number of citizens he successfully protected during the Athenian invasion of 349 BCE, with an estimated 1,000 people safeguarded in the face of overwhelming odds.

As a testament to his enduring legacy, the city of Mytilene still celebrates Chares of Mytilene as a national hero, with his likeness featured on various monuments and public art installations.
